The salt oven bakery

Down by the harbor, the salt oven bakery bakes bread that tastes of the sea. Fishermen stop there before dawn, when the first trays come out.

Dough and smoke

Every morning the baker salts the oven floor with coarse sea salt. The anchovies, the olives and the rosemary bread all share the salt oven's smoky crust.

The harbor gulls line the chimney until the smoke thins, then drift off across the masts toward the fish market.

By noon the bakery sells out, and the baker hangs a sign that says « mañana » — tomorrow, again.

ClipNotes fixture — the salt oven, a morning by the harbor.
